cues: Baroque composers wrote clarino parts that exploit its upper harmonics for brilliant, sustained lines.
In a brass choir, its upper voice can crown sustained chords with a clear, gleaming descant.
A short signal can announce an approaching procession, carrying clearly across an open square.
Jazz phrasing lets a player scoop into notes, lending a melody an expressive, speechlike inflection.
A high countermelody can emerge above strings at a climax, adding brilliance without taking over the tune.
In a ceremonial fanfare, sharply articulated calls give an entrance a sense of public occasion.
